players.product: Contracted hydro, wind, solar and battery-storage power for corporate and hyperscaler buyers, plus Westinghouse nuclear fuel, services and AP1000 reactors

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's Q2 2026 interim report: operating capacity was 48,676 MW at June 30, 2026 vs 47,549 MW a year earlier (approximately 48,700 MW, annualized long-term average generation of approximately 124,000 GWh, development pipeline of over 200 GW); approximately 8,300 MW of new development projects reached commercial operation in the past 12 months. Q2 proportionate actual renewable generation was 9,378 GWh vs 9,542 GWh (long-term average 10,151 GWh).
quarterly_data.figure: capacity 48,676 MW (vs 47,549 MW); ~8,300 MW commissioned in the last twelve months

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's Q2 2026 interim report, proportionate results by segment for Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025: hydroelectric revenue $543 million vs $457 million and Adjusted EBITDA $488 million vs $301 million (average revenue per MWh $75 vs $70; Colombia hydro generation 1,434 GWh vs 978 GWh at $90 vs $56 per MWh, on higher spot pricing from lower system-wide hydrology); wind revenue $141 million vs $146 million; utility-scale solar revenue $137 million vs $126 million; distributed energy & storage revenue $44 million vs $67 million; sustainable solutions revenue $153 million vs $178 million, with sustainable solutions FFO of $44 million vs $74 million as stronger results in Westinghouse, driven by growth in its operating plant services business and new plants business as global demand for nuclear power continues to accelerate, were more than offset by commercial initiatives that benefited the prior year. Total proportionate revenue $1,018 million vs $974 million; proportionate Adjusted EBITDA $831 million vs $700 million; consolidated revenues $1,710 million vs $1,692 million.
quarterly_data.figure: proportionate revenue $1,018 million (vs $974 million); Adjusted EBITDA $831 million (vs $700 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's Q2 2026 interim report, contract profile: contracted generation as a share of total proportionate generation is 93% for the rest of 2026, 92% in 2027, 90% in 2028, 88% in 2029 and 87% in 2030, at a price per MWh of $74, $76, $77, $78 and $79 respectively; the power portfolio has a weighted-average remaining contract duration of 12 years on a proportionate basis (13 years in North America, 17 years in Europe, 11 years in Brazil, 5 years in Colombia). Brazil and Colombia hydro are contracted approximately 90% and 70% of long-term average for the remainder of 2026. The economic exposure of contracted generation is power authorities (32%), distribution companies (23%), commercial & industrial users (35%) and Brookfield (10%); Brookfield Renewable sells electricity to Brookfield through a single long-term PPA across its New York hydroelectric facilities. Management expects rising power prices to be captured as Brazil and Colombia power is re-contracted over the medium term, and, based on current market prices for energy and ancillary products, a net positive impact to cash flows from the North American hydroelectric contracts that expire over the next five years.
quarterly_data.figure: 93% contracted rest of 2026; 92% 2027; 12-year weighted-average contract duration

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's Q2 2026 interim report: investment in the construction and development of solar, wind, distributed generation and battery energy storage projects was $1,326 million in Q2 2026 and $2,584 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026; capital expenditure commitments outstanding, primarily contracted project costs for growth initiatives, were $7,659 million at June 30, 2026 (December 31, 2025: $4,770 million), of which $3,036 million is payable in 2026, $2,947 million in 2027, $1,473 million in 2028 to 2030 and $203 million thereafter.
quarterly_data.figure: capex commitments $7,659 million (vs $4,770 million); Q2 construction investment $1,326 million

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's Q2 2026 interim report lists assets it agreed to acquire with institutional partners, subject to closing conditions: Boralex in Canada (utility-scale solar, wind, hydroelectric and battery energy storage; 8.2 GW development and 3.8 GW operating; Brookfield Renewable economic interest approximately 18%; expected close Q3 2026); a 2 GW battery energy storage development portfolio in China (8%, expected close Q3 2026); a 201 MW wind development in China (20%, H2 2026); and a 244 MW utility-scale solar development in South Korea (25%, Q1 2032).
quarterly_data.figure: Boralex: 3.8 GW operating, 8.2 GW development; ~18% economic interest
